question: European port activities represent an essential industrial tool for our economies, which cannot be reduced to the simple moving of goods. In its 2013 Communication entitled ‘Ports: an engine for growth’, the Commission already stressed that ‘investments are needed to adapt port infrastructure and facilities to suit new transport and logistics requirements and absorb the expected growth of cargo’.

In its ‘Integrated Maritime Policy’, the European Union has set itself the following objectives: ‘to enable the growth of maritime regions and coastal regions as regards shipping, seaports, shipbuilding, maritime jobs’. 1.
What has been the situation since then with regard to investment in European ports?
What measures have been taken to secure and develop jobs in ports, as announced in the Integrated Maritime Policy and other Commission communications?
answer: 1. The EU is supporting investments in ports through several instruments. The Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) has supported projects that develop and modernise basic port infrastructure, provide safe port access, strengthen the connections to maritime ports and ensure year-round navigability of EU waters with more than EUR 1.8 billion in grants.

The CEF Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Facility (AFIF) supports the deployment of infrastructure in ports, through an ongoing rolling-call with the total budget of EUR 1 billion. The Cohesion Fund and the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) financial support to maritime and inland waterway ports amounts to EUR 5.

2 billion in the period 2014-2027, in the areas of environment, clean energies and connection of ports to other modes of transport. 2. In its communication on a new approach for a sustainable blue economy (1), the Commission considers that, beyond transhipment and logistics, port future lies in roles as energy hubs, offshore renewable energy, circular economy and industrial clusters.

While employment in the port sector has generally remained stable between 2009 and 202 0 (2), taking up these new roles will improve job opportunities. The European Skills Agenda (3) supports upskilling and reskilling, while several EU funds (4) invest in people, jobs and skills supporting ports and the blue economy.
